Once a person has been granted a 'wish' by the SCP, it has no effect on them for at least 4 years (longest recorded time between a previously affected person being affected and touching the SCP again).

That parenthetical speaks to the longest lag time, not the least. It also, as currently phrased, doesn't establish anything about the effect; just describes one particular instance of a multiple-user over a long interval.

Not going to correct this because I'm not really clear on what the author intended to say in the first place.

item.content:encoded:
I like this, just one small nitpick:

The agent died after 2 weeks of total sleep deprivation. Wikipedia has this to say about Fatal familial insomnia:

Complete inability to sleep is followed by rapid loss of weight. This lasts for about three months.
Dementia, during which the patient becomes unresponsive or mute over the course of six months. This is the final progression of the disease, after which death follows.

So that is 9 months of being without any sleep before you die, on avarage.

Anywayz, still worth an upvote

item.content:encoded:
Umm… Yeah… This is Safe. Leave it in its box and follow the relatively simple containment protocols, and you're good.

Also, this is worded oddly:

Once a person has been granted a 'wish' by the SCP, it has no effect on them for at least 4 years (longest recorded time between a previously affected person being affected and touching the SCP again).

Did they have someone try using it again once a week for four years until it worked again? The way it's worded sounds more like… I'm not sure, actually. But if it's trying to factually state the minimum duration between uses which can possibly be achieved… I'd say just drop the parenthetical. Maybe something like:

Once a person has been granted a 'wish' in this manner, SCP-810 cannot have any further effect on that person for at least four years.

Gonna downvote this one. Some more minor things, such as just being difficult to read/unclear in some spots, and the class being wrong. Then stuff like the Agent dying from sleep deprivation itself (instead of complications arising from it), or instead of dying he just has to take heavy sleeping pill dosages (and effectively be forced to do so since he has no desire to sleep anymore), or something.

No. The only thing that makes it at all dangerous after containment is that they keep experimenting with it. If you just cease experimentation (after termination of any Class-D who was unfortunate enough to have been subject to it), keep it monitored, etc., it shouldn't need to be any more than Safe.

I'm not going to upvote this just yet, but I really like the idea. It relies on the assumption that "you'll never want for X" means "You'll never be without X", when it really means "You will never have any motivation to get X".
